test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 13 Jan 2021 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: In which year did the voting age for the Lok Sabha and the State Legislative Assembly elections change from 21 to 18 years?
solution:
The correct answer is **__1988.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In India, the voting age has been reduced from** 21 years to 18 years by the 61st Constitutional Amendment Act, 1988.**
 
• It comes into force by amending** Article 326.**
 
• The bill was passed by the** Lok Sabha on 15th December 1988.**
 
• The bill was passed by the** Rajya Sabha on 20th December 1988**.
 
• The bill was assented by **President Venkaraman on 28th March 1989.**
 
• The bill came into force on** 28th March 1989.**
 
• The Prime Minister who reduced the voting age from** 21 to 18 years - Rajiv Gandhi.**
 
• The first general elections to the Lok Sabha were held in India - **Between 25th October 1951 and 21st February 1952**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Article 326:**

 
 
• The Constitution provides that the elections to the House of the People and to the Legislative Assembly of every State shall be on the basis of adult suffrage.
 
 
 
• **Article 324:**
 
 
• ​Article 324 of the Indian Constitution deals it the power and authority to conduct, control, and supervise the entire election process in the country including elections to the Parliament, the Legislatures of every state, and to the offices of the President and Vice-President.
